Subject: Acme MSA redlines — indemnity / IP section

Connor,

Please find attached our redline to the MSA and proposed order form language. Our main open items are:
- Customer control of defense for third-party IP claims (we normally require choice of counsel and settlement approval);
- Broad definition of IP claim to include contributor/OSS claims — we want explicit carveouts;
- A cap and deductible for indemnity recoveries.

We’d like to resolve these before we execute the order form next week. Paul (cc'd) will handle legal details — happy to set a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Rebecca Li
Contracts Manager | Acme Payments
Acme Payments

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MSA redlines — indemnity / IP section

Thanks Rebecca — saw the redline. High level thoughts:

- Redwood position: we are comfortable indemnifying for third-party claims alleging IP infringement that arise from our deliverables/services, subject to:
  * We have sole control of the defense and settlement (but we will not agree to terms that permit settling a claim that admits the customer's liability or imposes an ongoing obligation on the customer without their consent).
  * Timely notice and cooperation obligations from the customer (we need notice within 30 days so we can evaluate).
  * Limitations: indemnity liability should be capped (order form level) and exclude claims arising from customer's modifications, combination with third-party tech, or customer's data.

- OSS/open-source: we can provide a limited warranty that our deliverables don't intentionally violate OSS licenses, but mass OSS indemnities are a non-starter. We can agree to reasonable OSS carveouts and a remediation path.

- Cap / deductible: propose order-form cap = 3x annual fees and a per-claim deductible of $50k for third-party IP claims; open to negotiation.

I'll attach an internal suggested markup for legal (RWI_indemnity_suggested_markups_20261012.docx). Marissa — can you review the OSS carveouts and defense-control language below and advise if we can accept customer settlement-approval language with a narrow approval right?

Proposed short clause (for discussion):
"Redwood shall have the right to assume control of the defense of any third party claim alleging that the Services infringe any third party's intellectual property, provided that Redwood shall not settle any claim in a manner that materially affects Customer's rights or imposes any ongoing monetary or injunctive obligation on Customer without Customer's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld."

Happy to take a call tomorrow afternoon. Karthik — FYI in case Acme presses on commercial tradeoffs.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Paul Barnes <paul.barnes@barnes-cole.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Rebecca Li <contracts@acmepayments.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MSA redlines — indemnity / IP section

Connor — appreciate the quick reply. A few points from Acme's side:

- Choice of counsel: Acme is not comfortable with Redwood having unilateral choice of counsel for claims that materially impact Acme. We are open to Redwood leading defense but require that counsel be reasonably acceptable to Acme and that Acme has the right to participate with its own counsel at its own cost.
- Settlement control: we need to ensure settlements do not release Redwood from obligations or strip Acme of remedies without Acme's consent — the current formulation is too open.
- OSS: our redline simply tries to preserve Acme's ability to assert a claim if an OSS contributor asserts infringement. We can accept a remediation-first approach but need some explicit obligation for Redwood to remediate or replace infringing components.

Attached is our counter language with limited edits. If we can get to a middle ground on caps and the counsel/settlement controls, Acme is prepared to finalize the order form this week.

Paul
Barnes & Cole LLP (external counsel for Acme)

Forwarding Acme's counsel reply — highlights below and suggested internal compromise for legal approval before I send a new markup:

Key asks from Acme:
- Reasonable approval of counsel (they want a say)
- Settlement approval right when settlement would bind Acme or affect its business
- OSS remediation obligation

Suggested compromise (for Marissa):
- Redwood to have initial right to control defense with counsel selected by Redwood; Customer may reasonably object to counsel on conflict grounds within 10 business days. If a material conflict exists or Redwood fails to control defense (no action within 30 days), Customer may assume control.
- Settlement: require Redwood to obtain Customer's written consent for settlements that impose payment obligations, admissions of liability, or injunctive relief affecting Customer; consent not to be unreasonably withheld where settlement includes a release solely of Redwood's liability for the asserted claim.
- OSS: include remediation/replace clause with a good-faith schedule and, if remediation is not feasible, reasonably metric-based credits or termination rights limited to affected components.
- Cap: move to 3x annual fees but remain open to 2x if we can tighten exclusions (customer-caused issues, combined-use).

Ask: Marissa, please prepare a final markup with language we can send back to Paul. Also flag if the proposed acceptance of "consent not to be unreasonably withheld" on settlement is risky from a legal precedent perspective. Karthik: if we need to move the cap for commercial reasons, what’s our walkaway?

Attachments: RWI_indemnity_suggested_markups_20261012.docx

Thanks,
Connor
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MSA redlines — indemnity / IP section (final legal markup)

Connor / team / Paul — thanks for the summaries. Attached is Redwood's final suggested markup. High-level callouts:

- Defense control: we will accept primary defense control for IP infringement claims, subject to (i) Customer's right to reasonably object to counsel on conflict grounds, (ii) Customer's right to assume defense if Redwood fails to reasonably defend within 30 days, and (iii) Redwood's obligation to keep Customer informed.
- Settlement: we will not settle in a way that imposes ongoing obligations or admissions on Customer without written consent. We can agree to a requirement that Redwood obtain Customer consent for settlements that impose payment obligations or injunctive relief on Customer; we will agree that consent shall not be unreasonably withheld where the settlement contains a release solely of Redwood's liability.
- OSS / open-source: Redwood proposes a remediation-first obligation (use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate or replace) with a fallback of a limited credit or replacement solution. We cannot accept a broad indemnity for OSS contributor claims.
- Cap/ded: recommend 3x annual fees cap with carveouts (customer modifications, combined technology, third-party data). If Acme insists on 2x, require narrower scope or higher deductible ($100k).

I have included specific redline text in the attached file. If Acme reviews and confirms the few remaining commercial points (cap and deductible), I think we can finalize the order form without escalating. If they push on unconditional choice of counsel or broad OSS indemnities, we'll need to escalate.
